inconsistencies: #34533 and #36330 solve the same problem (wallet rebroadcast under -privatebroadcast leaking transaction origin) in mutually exclusive ways: #34533 reroutes rebroadcasts through private broadcast, #36330 suppresses them. They must be decided together; review #34533 first as the fuller fix, then #36330 as the minimal alternative.

Chain: #36628 is the base reimplementation and #36608 extends it with package relay and the CLI tool; #36628 must be reviewed first. #36608 also largely subsumes #36628's content, so a decision on which to carry forward is needed before either gets deep review.

The private-broadcast reimplementation (#36628/#36608) removes the node-state design that #34271, #34322, #36477, #36566, #36607, #36429, #34533 and #36330 all build on. A concept decision on the rewrite should precede review of those incremental fixes, or most of that review effort is wasted.
Chain: #36506 declares a dependency on #36437 and re-implements its orphan-reassignment fix plus three more holes; review #36437 first, then #36506 as the superset.

#36486 fixes the txid==wtxid ForgetTxHash hole that #36506 also fixes via typed forgetting in TxRequestTracker. These are duplicate fixes for one bug; pick one (prefer #36506's typed approach if that PR advances, otherwise #36486 as the targeted fix).
Chain: #36787 caches the serialized compact block message and is the stated prerequisite of #35558's prefilling; reviewing #35558 first is not useful.
Chain: #36607 depends on #36477 retaining finished private-broadcast records; #36477 is the lower-value PR but gates the P1, hence its position.

#36244, #36445, #35561 and #34824 all reduce cs_main acquisition or lock scope in net_processing and touch overlapping code. #36244 is the most invasive and will likely conflict with the other three; agree on sequencing before reviewing them in parallel.

#35502 (ProcessMessage) and #35522 (SendMessages) are both move-only splits of net_processing and overlap with #34824's restructuring of tx-relay state; they should be merged in a fixed order to avoid repeated rebases.

#30988 (SockMan split), #35040 (LocalAddressManager) and #34824 are all parts of the same net/net_processing restructuring effort (#30694, #33958); they are not duplicates but their landing order matters.

#35591 is an explicitly DO-NOT-MERGE integration branch; the Erlay work that is actually reviewable arrives as separate split-out PRs, so review time spent on the branch itself does not advance the protocol.
#36727 backports commits already merged to master; it carries no new p2p design decision, only release-branch assembly.
result.notes: The category is dominated by two clusters that drive most of the P1/P2 mass: private broadcast (nine PRs, several of which conflict or would be obsoleted by the #36628/#36608 rewrite) and 1p1c/orphan relay liveness (#36437, #36506, #36486, #36328). Deciding the private-broadcast architecture and the #36437/#36506 chain would resolve the ordering of roughly a sixth of the list. Remote-triggerable memory/DoS fixes (#36015, #36521, #35888) are kept at the very top because the category ranks attack resistance first; measured performance work (#36244, #35558, #36548, #36445) sits in P2 below correctness and liveness, and the net_processing refactor family is spread across P2/P3 according to whether it retires a concrete hazard or only improves readability.
